p.note: Neither Micron nor the Japanese government publishes the site's electricity use in MWh. The Micron 2026 Sustainability Report gives only company totals. This value is back-calculated from the disclosed site CO2. EEGS FY2023 (Apr 2023-Mar 2024) for FAB15: total GHG 1,108,474 t, energy-origin CO2 844,033 t. Assumptions: (a) grid factor = Chugoku Electric basic factor 0.511 kgCO2/kWh (FY2023 actual); (b) the fuel-to-electricity energy ratio matches Micron's global FY25 mix, 2,454,135 / 9,791,521 = 0.2506 MWh fuel per MWh electricity; (c) fuel is city gas at about 0.180 tCO2/MWh. Electricity = 844,033 / (0.511 + 0.2506 x 0.180) = 1,517,800 MWh, and 1,517,800 / 8760 = 173.3 MW. Upper-leaning variant (all energy CO2 from electricity): 844,033 / 0.000511 = 1,651,700 MWh, or 188.6 MW. Treat the range as roughly 170-190 MW, and more uncertain than that if Micron buys from a retailer with a different emission factor. For context, Micron company-wide electricity in FY25 was 9,791,521 MWh (1,118 MW), so FAB15 would be about 15% of the company.

p.source: Intel - Explore Intel site environmental performance pages (Ocotillo and Chandler campuses, calendar-year 2024 data)
p.note: Site 'Energy Used' for CY2024: Ocotillo campus 2,111,443 MWh (https://www.exploreintel.com/ocotillo) plus Chandler campus 243,936 MWh (https://www.exploreintel.com/chandler) = 2,355,379 MWh. 2,355,379 / 8760 = 268.9 MW. Caveat: Intel's corporate 'energy use' metric includes electricity, gas and diesel, so this site figure probably includes natural gas. Electricity-only estimate: the NIST Draft Environmental Assessment for Intel Ocotillo (July 2024) says Ocotillo used about 15,800,000 therms of gas in 2023. At 29.3071 kWh/therm that is 463,052 MWh, giving (2,355,379 - 463,052) / 8760 = 216.0 MW. That still includes the Chandler campus's unknown gas use, so it leans high. Same EA: Fab 42 alone has an estimated maximum demand of 1.7 GWh/day (70.8 MW), and SRP's High-Tech Interconnection Project provides about 630 MW of load-serving capacity (all phases done April 2024). Renewable electricity: 98%.

g.source: Intel - 2024-25 Corporate Responsibility Report Executive Summary (key metrics table)
g.note: COMPANY-level proxy. Intel energy use (electricity, gas and diesel) went from 10.8 billion kWh (2023) to 11.4 billion kWh (2024): 11.4 / 10.8 - 1 = +5.6%. The earlier series was 10.6 (2020), 11.6 (2021), 10.9 (2022), so it is flat-to-noisy. Site-specific projection: the NIST Draft EA (July 2024, https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2024/07/08/Intel%20Ocotillo%20EA_DRAFT%20FINAL_VOLUME%201%208July2024.pdf) puts full-production demand for Fabs 42+52+62 at 8.5 GWh/day, or 354 MW. That is 1.7 GWh/day for Fab 42 and an estimated 3.4 GWh/day each for the new Fabs 52 and 62. So the ramp of Fabs 52 and 62 could add up to about 283 MW over several years, but the ramp timing is not disclosed.
